name: Low-gain antenna
description: A simple antenna that works in any direction. Slow, especially far from Earth.

name: Medium-gain antenna
description: A good antenna for missions near Earth and the Moon.

name: High-gain dish
description: A big dish that must point right at Earth. The only way to send lots of data from deep space.

name: Storage 32 Gb
description: Onboard memory that holds data until it can be sent to Earth.

name: Storage 256 Gb
description: More memory, so less data is lost when Earth is out of contact.

name: Basic ground station
description: One ground antenna. You can talk to the spacecraft about 4 hours a day.

name: Deep-space network (3 sites)
description: Three big antennas spread around the world, so one can always see the spacecraft. About 10 hours a day of contact are shared with your mission.
